basics.name: MD. Basim Al Zabir Shammo
basics.label: Aspiring Researcher in Robotic Systems and Machine Learning Applications
basics.summary: My research experience includes developing ML-based diagnostic systems across multiple domains. While my primary focus is robotics and autonomous systems, I have also contributed to healthcare ML projects. This cross-domain experience has been invaluable for me. Working with noisy signals taught me feature engineering and classification under uncertainty, which is directly applicable to sensor-based fault detection in robotics, where sensor noise, drift, and failures are constant challenges.

publications.name: A Machine Learning Framework for Stress Detection Using Photoplethysmography (PPG) Signals
publications.summary: Investigated advanced feature engineering and classification techniques to detect stress levels from non-invasive PPG sensor data, achieving high accuracy in real-world signal conditions.

publications.name: Real-Time RFID Authentication and Access Control System with Networked Logging
publications.summary: Designed and implemented a secure, networked access control system using RFID technology, focusing on low-latency authentication and centralized activity monitoring.

publications.name: Predicting Fear-Related Nightmares in Children Using Traditional Machine Learning Models
publications.summary: Applied ensemble learning and regression models to identify physiological and behavioral patterns preceding nightmares in pediatric subjects.

publications.name: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Nightmares in Children: A Pediatric Psychological Integration
publications.summary: Explored the integration of psychological assessments with sensor-based data to build a holistic predictive framework for childhood sleep disorders.

publications.name: Vehicle Classification and Detection Using YOLOv8: A Study on Highway Traffic Analysis
publications.summary: Utilized the state-of-the-art YOLOv8 architecture for high-speed vehicle detection and multi-class categorization in complex highway environments.
